item.description:
Koan 0.1.6

  • Sync, through your own iCloud. Settings ▸ Sync is off until you turn it on. With it on, your workspaces, pinned tabs, folders, essentials and bookmarks are the same on every Mac signed in to your Apple Account. History and a list of each Mac's open tabs are separate switches, off to begin with; Library ▸ Other Devices shows what's open elsewhere. Private windows, passwords and website data never sync. Koan has no servers of its own: the data sits in your iCloud, where only you can read it. The welcome flow offers the switch to new installs.
  • When sync can't run, it says why. Not signed in to iCloud, iCloud Drive off, storage full, no network: each has its own sentence in Settings ▸ Sync instead of an error code.
  • Compact mode with hundreds of tabs. Sliding the sidebar in and out had become slower in 0.1.5 for workspaces of several hundred tabs. It is smooth again: about a third less time per frame at 300 tabs.
  • Saved logins and AutoFill move to a newer keychain. The first launch of this version moves Koan's saved logins, AutoFill details and live-folder token from the login keychain to the Mac's data-protection keychain. Nothing to do, and nothing should ask for a password.
  • Bookmarks arriving by sync keep their dates, so sorting by date added is the same on every Mac.

Koan 0.1.5

  • Pages run faster. One of Koan's own page scripts was slowing every click and keypress on every site. On Speedometer 3.1 Koan went from 23% behind Safari to about 5% behind. Pages with many images also load faster with content blocking on.
  • Links that open other apps. A link meant for another app (Slack, Zoom, Teams, VS Code, Mail) used to do nothing. Koan now asks "Open this link in Slack?" and hands it over; tick "Always open Slack links from this site" and it won't ask again. A tab that was opened only to launch the app closes itself. Settings ▸ Privacy & Security has the switch and the list of sites you've allowed.
  • Tab size. Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Tab size: Compact is the sidebar as it was; Comfortable makes the rows, titles and icons a little larger.
  • The sidebar follows you. When you switch to a tab that isn't in view (⌃Tab, ⌘T, ⌘1–9, a link that opens in front), the list scrolls just enough to show it. It stays put while you're scrolling or dragging, and for tabs opened in the background.
  • Hundreds of tabs cost much less. In a workspace of a hundred tabs or more, Koan builds only the rows near the part of the sidebar you can see. With 300 tabs it uses about 70 MB less memory, starts sooner, and switching workspaces and compact mode are several times smoother.
  • History and Bookmarks. On macOS 26 these lists could ignore a scroll or take seconds to respond when they were long. They are built differently now, use less memory and scroll faster.

Koan 0.1.4

  • A tab switcher. Hold ⌃ and press Tab: a panel shows your tabs as page previews, most recently used first. Keep pressing Tab (or the arrow keys) to move, let go of ⌃ to switch, Esc to cancel, W to close the highlighted tab. A quick ⌃Tab goes straight back to the tab you were just on. Settings ▸ Tabs ▸ Tab Switching chooses between recently used and sidebar order, and whether the panel shows.
  • Middle click. A middle click on a tab closes it, as ⌘W would. On a link, a bookmark, a history row or the back and forward buttons it opens the page in a background tab. On empty sidebar space it opens a new tab.
  • Other keyboards. On German, French, Swiss, Nordic and Italian keyboards the next and previous tab shortcuts (⇧⌘] and ⇧⌘[) couldn't be pressed. They now sit on the keys macOS moves them to, and Settings ▸ Shortcuts says where each shortcut is on your keyboard.
  • Full screen. The sidebar's toolbar no longer leaves a gap where the window buttons were, and a sidebar on the right no longer keeps an empty strip above the page.
  • Dragging a tab to another window. The window it left now moves on to the tab that was next to it, and never lands on a tab the other window is showing.
  • Smaller fixes. A link opened from a glance in a private window stays in that window. With Reduce Motion on, the welcome steps, folder rows and a web app's command bar fade instead of sliding. The extensions overflow button has a proper name for VoiceOver.

Koan 0.1.3

  • Fixes a freeze. On macOS 26, Koan could lock up completely, taking no clicks and refusing to quit, when the tab list in the sidebar jumped a long way at once. The list is built differently now and can't get stuck that way.
  • Koan no longer stays frozen. If it ever stops responding for thirty seconds while working flat out, it now ends itself so you can reopen it with your windows and tabs as they were, instead of sitting there until it is force-quit.

Koan 0.1.2

  • Short work addresses. Typing a name and a slash, like wiki/, opens that address on your network instead of searching for it. Once a name has loaded, longer addresses under it (go/roadmap) open too.
  • Scroll bars match the page. A site that has a dark design but shows itself light, such as an encyclopedia set to Light, no longer gets a dark scroll bar beside a white page, and the scroll bar follows when you change the site's own theme.
  • The camera and microphone indicator now reads properly to VoiceOver.

Koan 0.1.1

  • A smoother sidebar. In compact mode the sidebar now glides in and out as one piece, and the page settles once instead of resizing as it goes.
  • Agents reach further. A click, menu or drop aimed at a sidebar row that is scrolled out of view now scrolls it into view first.

Koan 0.1.0

The first Koan: Safari's engine with Zen's sidebar.

  • A sidebar that is the browser. Workspaces with their own colours, essentials, pinned tabs, nested folders and live folders that follow a feed or a GitHub repository. Collapse it to icons, put it on either side, or hide it in compact mode.
  • More than one page at a time. Split view with up to four panes, and Glance for a quick look at a link without leaving the page.
  • Reading. Reader mode, find in page, on-device translation, page zoom remembered per site, and Hide Distracting Items.
  • Private by default. Trackers and ads are blocked, sites ask before using the camera, microphone or location, private windows leave nothing behind, and Koan sends no telemetry.
  • Kept apart. Containers give a workspace its own sign-ins; profiles are separate Koans with their own everything.
  • Your things come with you. Import tabs, bookmarks and history from Zen, Chrome, Arc and Safari. History and bookmarks are searchable from the address bar.
  • Passwords and AutoFill. Saved logins, contact details and cards are kept in your keychain and filled with Touch ID.
  • Extensions and web apps. Safari and Chrome web extensions run in Koan, and any site can open as an app in a window of its own.
  • Built for agents, when you want them. koan, a command-line tool and MCP server, ships inside the app and stays off until you turn it on in Settings.
  • Updates are signed and verified before they install.
